# Tako ID Streaming Overlay

> A collection of interactive, cyber-themed HTML overlays for displaying donation activity, music, polls, milestones, leaderboards, and sound effects on Tako ID-based live streams.

## Project Information

| Detail | Description |
|---|---|
| **Project name** | Tako ID Streaming Overlay |
| **Repository** | [himang-dg/takoidoverlay](https://github.com/himang-dg/takoidoverlay) |
| **Owner** | [Himang-DG](https://github.com/himang-dg) |
| **Category** | Streaming overlay / donation alert / live-stream UI |
| **Upload year** | 2026 |
| **Repository creation date** | May 8, 2026 |
| **Latest detected code update** | August 24, 2026 |
| **License** | Not yet specified |
| **Main language** | HTML |
| **GitHub language composition** | HTML 100% |
| **Repository status** | Public |
| **Live preview** | Cannot yet be confirmed as an active URL |
| **Original repository description** | `ada deh` |

## Project Summary

Tako ID Streaming Overlay is a set of HTML-based overlay templates designed to improve the visual appearance of live streams. These overlays display various real-time information related to viewer interaction, donations, music, polls, donation achievements, supporter rankings, and sound effects.

Each template is built with a modern cyber/neon look using a combination of dark colors, cyan, blue, and yellow accents. The templates are designed to be used on overlay systems that support dynamic placeholders with formats such as `{{gifterName}}`, `{{formattedAmount}}`, `{{rankings}}`, and `{{queue}}`.

This project focuses more on the visual presentation side and the viewer experience rather than backend development or data processing. The data is assumed to be sent by the Tako platform through placeholders, which are then processed by JavaScript inside each HTML file.

## Problems Solved

In live streaming, donation information and community activity are often only displayed as standard text. This can make the stream look less attractive and reduce the visual impact of viewer interactions.

This project solves several of these problems by providing:

- A more attractive and informative donation notification display.
- Real-time visualization of supporter activity.
- A display of the currently playing music along with its progress and queue.
- A representation of polls in the form of progress bars.
- A progress indicator for donation targets or milestones.
- A supporter ranking list through a leaderboard.
- A sound effect display that is livelier and matches the stream theme.
- Support for avatars, badges, stickers, donation amounts, and user information.
- Overlay components with a transparent background so they are easy to place on top of the live stream.

## Main Features

### 1. Donation Alert

File: [`DBangkongSNewTakoID/Alert.html`](https://github.com/himang-dg/takoidoverlay/blob/main/DBangkongSNewTakoID/Alert.html)

Displays donation notifications or supporter messages in the form of a cyber-themed overlay card.

Available features:

- Displays the message from the supporter.
- Displays the donation amount with a yellow glow effect.
- Displays the sender's name.
- Displays the sender's avatar.
- Displays the verified status.
- Displays supporter badges.
- Supports stickers using the `[sticker_name]` format.
- Hides the avatar if the URL is not available or the image fails to load.
- Hides the message if the placeholder does not have a value yet.
- Displays decorative images from external sources.
- Floating animation on the logo and decorations.
- Neon particle effects that move upward.
- A light effect that moves across the overlay card.

Main placeholders used:

```text
{{message}}
{{formattedAmount}}
{{gifterPicture}}
{{gifterName}}
{{isGifterVerified}}
{{gifterBadges}}
```

### 2. Supporter Leaderboard

File: [`DBangkongSNewTakoID/Leaderboard.html`](https://github.com/himang-dg/takoidoverlay/blob/main/DBangkongSNewTakoID/Leaderboard.html)

Displays a list of supporters based on their contribution ranking.

Available features:

- Displays the leaderboard title.
- Displays the supporter ranking.
- Special colors for first, second, and third place.
- Displays supporter avatars.
- Displays supporter names.
- Displays supporter badges.
- Displays the total contribution amount.
- Hover effect on each ranking row.
- Particle animation and visual decorations.
- Title fallback to `Leaderboard` if data is not available.

The leaderboard data is read from a JSON placeholder:

```text
{{rankings}}
```

Each ranking entry can contain information such as:

```javascript
{
  name,
  picture,
  badges,
  formattedAmount
}
```

### 3. Milestone Progress

File: [`DBangkongSNewTakoID/Milestone.html`](https://github.com/himang-dg/takoidoverlay/blob/main/DBangkongSNewTakoID/Milestone.html)

Displays the progress toward a donation target or a particular milestone.

Available features:

- Milestone title.
- Visual progress bar.
- Current progress value.
- Milestone target value.
- Progress percentage.
- Glow effect on the donation amount.
- The progress bar value is capped at a maximum of 100%.
- Title fallback to `Milestone`.
- Progress bar transition animation.
- Neon particle effects and cyan gradient.

Main placeholders:

```text
{{title}}
{{percentage}}
{{formattedStepProgress}}
{{formattedStepTarget}}
```

### 4. Polling Overlay

File: [`DBangkongSNewTakoID/Polling.html`](https://github.com/himang-dg/takoidoverlay/blob/main/DBangkongSNewTakoID/Polling.html)

Displays community poll results with a progress bar visualization based on the amount of contributions or votes for each option.

Available features:

- Displays the poll title.
- Displays the poll end time.
- Displays the list of poll options.
- Calculates the percentage of each option dynamically.
- Displays the amount or total contribution of each option.
- Displays the list of voters if available.
- Displays the total poll contribution.
- Uses the Indonesian currency format `IDR`.
- Title fallback to `Polling`.
- Hides the end time information if the data is not available.
- Progress bar animation and particle effects.

The poll data is read from a JSON placeholder:

```text
{{pollingOptions}}
```

Each option can contain:

```javascript
{
  name,
  totalAmount,
  formattedTotalAmount,
  voters
}
```

### 5. Song Share / Music Player

File: [`DBangkongSNewTakoID/SongShare.html`](https://github.com/himang-dg/takoidoverlay/blob/main/DBangkongSNewTakoID/SongShare.html)

Displays the song that is currently playing or requested by viewers through the song request system.

Available features:

- Displays the song title.
- Displays the artist name.
- Displays the cover art.
- Displays the song duration.
- Displays the playback progress.
- Displays the requester's name.
- Displays the requester's verified status.
- Displays the requester's badges.
- Displays the queue of upcoming songs.
- Displays the number of songs still in the queue.
- Displays an idle state when there is no song.
- Displays the pause status between songs.
- Displays error messages.
- Cover art fallback if the image fails to load.
- Parses queue data using JSON.
- Progress bar effect with a cyan and blue gradient.

Main placeholders:

```text
{{songTitle}}
{{songArtist}}
{{formattedElapsed}}
{{formattedDuration}}
{{progressPercent}}
{{songCoverArtUrl}}
{{requesterName}}
{{requesterPicture}}
{{requesterBadges}}
{{isRequesterVerified}}
{{isPlaying}}
{{isPaused}}
{{isInGap}}
{{gapText}}
{{error}}
{{queue}}
```

### 6. Soundboard Overlay

File: [`DBangkongSNewTakoID/Soundboard.html`](https://github.com/himang-dg/takoidoverlay/blob/main/DBangkongSNewTakoID/Soundboard.html)

Displays information about sound effects triggered by supporters or certain activities during the live stream.

Available features:

- Displays the sound effect name.
- Displays the sender's name.
- Displays the verified status.
- Displays the sender's badges.
- Sound name fallback to `Sound Effect`.
- SVG-based music icon.
- Neon particle effects.
- Running light effect on the card.
- Transparent display for streaming overlay needs.
- Badge fallback to a text tag if the icon fails to load.

Main placeholders:

```text
{{soundName}}
{{gifterName}}
{{isGifterVerified}}
{{gifterBadges}}
```

## Tech Stack

### HTML5

All components are built using HTML5 with a standard document structure:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
```

HTML is used as the foundation of every overlay template and serves as the container for the visual structure, data placeholders, and interactive scripts.

### Tailwind CSS Browser CDN

The project uses Tailwind CSS through the browser CDN:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tailwindcss/browser@4"></script>
```

Tailwind is used for:

- Flexbox layout.
- Spacing and padding.
- Background colors.
- Borders and rounded corners.
- Typography.
- Element sizes.
- Positioning.
- Basic responsiveness.
- Utility classes to build components quickly.

The project does not use a Tailwind configuration file or a local build process. Styling is done directly using Tailwind utility classes and custom CSS inside each HTML file.

### Vanilla JavaScript

Interactivity is built using JavaScript without any additional framework.

JavaScript is used to:

- Read dynamic placeholders.
- Handle fallbacks when data is empty.
- Create HTML elements dynamically.
- Read JSON data.
- Calculate poll percentages.
- Build the leaderboard ranking.
- Build the song queue list.
- Control element visibility.
- Handle errors on external images.
- Display badges and avatars.
- Create visual particles randomly.

Example of the pattern used:

```javascript
window.addEventListener("load", () => {
  // Initialize the overlay after the whole page has loaded
});
```

### Custom CSS Animations

Besides Tailwind CSS, each overlay uses custom CSS to build its visual identity and animations.

The animations used include:

- `shine` for the light effect that moves across the card.
- `rise` for neon particles that move upward.
- `logoFloat` for the floating effect on the logo.
- `moneyGlow` for the donation amount.
- `decorFloat` for decorative images.
- Transitions for progress bar width changes.

### JSON Data Parsing

Several overlays read complex data from JSON placeholders, such as:

```html
<script id="rankings-data" type="application/json">
  {{rankings}}
</script>
```

This approach is used in:

- Leaderboard.
- Polling.
- Song Share queue.

The data is then processed using:

```javascript
JSON.parse(...)
```

### External Assets

The project uses several external assets, including:

- Tako ID assets.
- Supporter badges from `tako.id`.
- Stickers from `assets.tako.id`.
- Decorative images from the GitHub CDN.
- Logos and supporting images from external repositories.

Examples of external sources used:

```text
https://tako.id/images/badges/
https://assets.tako.id/
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/
```

## Repository Structure

```text
takoidoverlay/
├── README.md
└── DBangkongSNewTakoID/
    ├── Alert.html
    ├── Leaderboard.html
    ├── Milestone.html
    ├── Polling.html
    ├── SongShare.html
    └── Soundboard.html
```

### Structure Explanation

#### `README.md`

The README currently contains the repository title and a short description:

```text
# takoidoverlay
ada deh
```

#### `DBangkongSNewTakoID/`

The main directory containing all the HTML overlay templates.

| File | Function |
|---|---|
| `Alert.html` | Donation notifications and supporter messages |
| `Leaderboard.html` | Supporter ranking based on contribution |
| `Milestone.html` | Donation target or milestone progress |
| `Polling.html` | Community poll results |
| `SongShare.html` | Song player and request queue |
| `Soundboard.html` | Sound effect notifications |

## System Workflow

In general, each overlay works with the following flow:

1. The streaming platform or the Tako system provides values for the placeholders.
2. The HTML file receives the data through template variables such as `{{gifterName}}`.
3. The browser loads Tailwind CSS from the CDN.
4. JavaScript runs after the `load` event.
5. Placeholders are checked to determine whether data is available.
6. Certain elements are shown, hidden, or filled dynamically.
7. JSON data such as rankings, polling options, and the queue is processed with `JSON.parse`.
8. The overlay displays the final result in the form of a transparent card with animations.

Example of the data flow in `Polling.html`:

```text
{{pollingOptions}}
        ↓
JSON.parse(...)
        ↓
Total contribution calculation
        ↓
Percentage calculation for each option
        ↓
Progress bar creation
        ↓
Polling overlay is displayed
```

## Visual Characteristics

The visual identity of the project uses a cyber/neon style with several consistent elements:

- Slate-based dark background.
- Transparent cyan borders.
- Cyan and blue gradients.
- Yellow highlights for donation amounts.
- Rounded cards with a large radius.
- Drop shadow and glow.
- Glowing particles.
- Horizontal shine effect.
- Floating animation on the logo and decorations.
- Transparent background for integration with the live stream.

The dominant color palette:

```text
Slate / dark background : #0f172a
Cyan                    : #22d3ee
Blue                    : #60a5fa
Yellow donation glow    : #facc15
Muted text              : #94a3b8
```

## How to Use

This repository does not have a `package.json`, build system, backend, or local server. Each HTML file can be used directly as an overlay template on platforms that support custom HTML overlays.

General usage steps:

1. Open one of the overlay files.
2. Copy the HTML content into the overlay system being used.
3. Make sure the platform provides the matching placeholders.
4. Adjust the asset URLs, sizes, and colors if needed.
5. Connect the overlay to donation, polling, music, or sound effect events.
6. Test each placeholder using simulated data.
7. Place the overlay in the live streaming scene.

To simply view the basic appearance locally:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/himang-dg/takoidoverlay.git
cd takoidoverlay
```

Then open one of the following files using a browser:

```text
DBangkongSNewTakoID/Alert.html
DBangkongSNewTakoID/Leaderboard.html
DBangkongSNewTakoID/Milestone.html
DBangkongSNewTakoID/Polling.html
DBangkongSNewTakoID/SongShare.html
DBangkongSNewTakoID/Soundboard.html
```

Some data will not be fully displayed if the file is opened standalone because placeholders such as `{{gifterName}}`, `{{rankings}}`, or `{{queue}}` only have values when processed by the appropriate overlay platform.

## Technical Value of the Project

This project demonstrates several technical skills:

- Building custom overlay UIs for live streaming needs.
- Developing visual components with HTML and CSS.
- Using Tailwind CSS through a CDN.
- Creating custom animations using CSS keyframes.
- Processing dynamic data using Vanilla JavaScript.
- Processing JSON data from template variables.
- Creating fallbacks for empty or invalid data.
- Handling external image loading failures.
- Building reusable components for various live streaming events.
- Combining real-time data with an attractive visual display.
- Designing a transparent UI that can integrate with streaming software.

## Identified Limitations

Based on the current contents of the repository:

- There is no complete usage documentation yet.
- There are no official screenshots or demo previews yet.
- There is no build configuration yet.
- There are no automated tests yet.
- There is no backend or internal API yet.
- The data depends heavily on placeholders from an external platform.
- Some assets are loaded from external URLs.
- There is no license file yet.
- There is no GitHub Actions configuration yet.
- It cannot yet be confirmed whether GitHub Pages is active as a live preview.
- The JSON fallback in some files still depends on valid data from the calling system.

## Short Description for the Portfolio Card

### Indonesian Version

**Tako ID Streaming Overlay** adalah kumpulan overlay HTML interaktif untuk live streaming yang menampilkan donation alert, leaderboard supporter, milestone progress, polling, music request, dan sound effect. Proyek ini menggunakan HTML5, Tailwind CSS melalui CDN, Vanilla JavaScript, custom CSS animations, serta JSON parsing untuk memproses data dinamis dari platform Tako ID.

### English Version

**Tako ID Streaming Overlay** is a collection of interactive HTML overlays for live streaming. It provides donation alerts, supporter leaderboards, milestone progress, polls, music requests, and sound effect notifications. The project uses HTML5, Tailwind CSS via CDN, Vanilla JavaScript, custom CSS animations, and JSON parsing to render dynamic data from the Tako ID platform.

## Short Tech Stack

```text
HTML5
Tailwind CSS v4 Browser CDN
Vanilla JavaScript
Custom CSS Animations
JSON Parsing
External CDN Assets
Tako ID Overlay Template Variables
```

## Project Status

This project serves as a collection of visual overlay templates for live streaming needs. The main development focus is on interface design, animation, dynamic placeholder integration, and visualization of viewer interaction data.

Further development that can be done:

- Add screenshots for each overlay.

- Add safer JSON validation.
- Add fallbacks for invalid data.
- Separate CSS and JavaScript into structured files.
- Add theme configuration.
- Add a responsive mode for various streaming resolutions.
- Add a license file.
- Provide a demo page using GitHub Pages.

PartyNeraka.content: # PartyNeraka ![](/images/party-neraka/partyneraka-1.webp) ![](/images/party-neraka/partyneraka-2.webp) ![](/images/party-neraka/partyneraka-3.webp) ![](/images/party-neraka/partyneraka-4.webp) > A community website and streamer directory for Party Neraka with a visual concept themed around hell, horror, fire, and local humor. ## Project Information | Detail | Description | |---|---| | **Project name** | PartyNeraka | | **Category** | Community Website / Streamer Directory / Landing Page | | **Status** | Public | | **Upload year** | 2026 | | **Created on GitHub** | May 15, 2026 | | **Latest detected update** | August 24, 2026 | | **Repository** | [github.com/himang-dg/PartyNeraka](https://github.com/himang-dg/PartyNeraka) | | **Live Preview** | [partyneraka.vercel.app](https://partyneraka.vercel.app/) | | **Project owner** | [Himang](https://github.com/himang-dg) | | **License** | Not yet specified in the repository | | **Main language** | TypeScript | --- ## Project Summary PartyNeraka is a community website that serves as a directory of streamers and content creators who are part of the Party Neraka ecosystem. The website presents the profiles of around 30 streamers in the form of interactive cards complete with photos, character descriptions, and links to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, as well as support or donation links. This project combines the concept of a streamer community with a dark fantasy and "hell" themed visual identity. The website's look is built using dark red, black, fire effects, embers, glow, transition animations, and horror-style typography to create a distinctive and easily recognizable visual experience. Besides the streamer directory, the website also provides a gallery section, official merchandise promotion, community social media links, admin contacts, and community support links. --- ## Problems Solved Before there was a centralized website, information about the streamers and creators in the community was potentially scattered across various platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and donation platforms. PartyNeraka addresses the following needs: - Provides one centralized place to get to know all the community's streamers. - Makes it easy for visitors to find each streamer's social media accounts. - Makes it easier for the audience to give support through donation platforms. - Builds an official digital identity for the Party Neraka community. - Displays streamer profiles in a more attractive way than an ordinary list of links. - Serves as a promotional medium for the community's official merchandise. - Provides a visual gallery to strengthen the branding and atmosphere of the community. - Creates a more interactive exploration experience through search, animations, hover effects, and load more. --- ## Main Functions ### 1. Streamer Directory The website displays the list of Party Neraka streamers in a card grid. Each card contains: - Streamer name. - Profile photo. - A description with a hell-themed humor style. - Instagram link. - TikTok link. - YouTube link. - Support or donation button. Streamer data is stored in a structured way in the file: ```text src/data/streamers.ts ``` Each streamer entry uses a TypeScript interface with the properties: ```text nama foto ig tiktok youtube donasi deskripsi ``` ### 2. Streamer Search Visitors can search for streamers by name through the search bar. Search features: - Runs directly on the client side. - Uses case-insensitive name matching. - Uses `useMemo` to optimize the filtering process. - Displays a special message when streamer data is not found. - Resets the number of displayed items when a new search is performed. ### 3. Load More Initially, the website displays eight streamers. Visitors can press the "Lihat Penghuni Lainnya..." ("See Other Residents...") button to display the next eight streamers. This approach helps keep the page looking concise and avoids displaying all the data at once. ### 4. Profiles and External Links Each streamer has direct links to their platforms. These links are opened in a new tab using: ```tsx target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" ``` The connected platforms include: - Instagram. - TikTok. - YouTube. - Tako. - Tiptap. ### 5. Interactive Animations The website uses Framer Motion to produce various visual interactions, such as: - Fade-in animation. - Slide-up animation. - Scale animation. - Hover animation. - Staggered entrance animation. - Animation when elements enter the viewport. - Pulsing logo animation. - Streamer card animation. - Gallery animation. - Marketplace banner animation. ### 6. Fire Embers Effect The `FireEmbers` component dynamically creates around 40 fire ember particles on the client side. Each ember has different characteristics: - Random horizontal position. - Random size. - Random animation delay. - Random animation duration. - Red glow effect. - Vertical movement from bottom to top. The randomization is done inside `useEffect` so that it does not cause a hydration mismatch in Next.js. ### 7. Gallery The website provides a gallery section containing several visual assets of the community. The gallery uses: - A masonry layout based on CSS columns. - A grayscale effect by default. - A color effect on hover. - Scale and fade-in animations. - Red borders matching the website's visual identity. Gallery data is managed through: ```text src/data/gallery.ts ``` ### 8. Merchandise Marketplace The `Neraka Store` section serves as a promotion for Party Neraka's official merchandise. This feature provides: - A merchandise promotion title. - A short description. - A button leading to the Shopee marketplace. - A shopping cart icon. - Hover and tap animations. - Floating and glow effects. The marketplace used: ```text https://shopee.co.id/partyneraka ``` ### 9. Community Social Media The website header provides direct access to: - Party Neraka's Instagram. - Party Neraka's TikTok. - The community Discord. - The community support link through Tako. ### 10. Admin Contact The footer displays the community's contact information: - Admin email. - WhatsApp number. - Developer profile link. - Party Neraka logo. - Dynamic copyright based on the current year. --- ## Main Features - Full-screen landing page with Party Neraka branding. - A directory of around 30 streamers. - Real-time streamer search. - Load more for the streamer list. - Interactive profile cards. - Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and donation links. - Community gallery. - Official merchandise promotion. - Discord community link integration. - Social media link integration. - Admin email and WhatsApp contact. - Dark theme with a horror and inferno style. - Moving embers or fire particle effect. - Glow effect and flickering fire text. - Scroll-based animations using Framer Motion. - Hover effects on cards, images, icons, and buttons. - Responsive layout for mobile, tablet, and desktop. - Fallback image when a streamer image fails to load. - Basic SEO metadata through the Next.js Metadata API. - Open Graph metadata for social sharing needs. - Twitter card metadata. - Custom fonts through `next/font/google`. - Type-safe data model using TypeScript. --- ## Tech Stack ### Core Technology - **TypeScript** - The main language for logic, components, and the data model. - **React 19** - The main library for building a component-based interface. - **Next.js 16** - The React framework used for routing, rendering, metadata, and application structure. - **Node.js / npm** - Runtime and package manager for development and the build process. ### Styling - **Tailwind CSS 4** - A utility-first CSS framework for building layout and styling. - **CSS Modules / Global CSS** - Custom styling for animations, colors, scrollbar, card effects, and utility classes. - **CSS Animations** - Used for the floating ember, fire flicker, pulse red, and glow effects. - **Glassmorphism** - Used on cards and several panels through transparency and backdrop blur effects. ### Animation - **Framer Motion 13** - Used for: - Entrance animation. - Scroll reveal. - Hover interaction. - Button interaction. - Layout animation. - Staggered animation. - Repeating logo animation. ### Icons and Typography - **React Icons** - Provides the Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Discord, WhatsApp, email, shopping cart, search, and support icons. - **Creepster** - A horror-themed font for headings and branding. - **Rajdhani** - The main font for body text and the interface. ### Tooling - **ESLint 9** - Code linting. - **eslint-config-next** - Next.js-specific linting configuration. - **PostCSS** - CSS processing for Tailwind CSS integration. - **TypeScript strict mode** - Helps maintain type safety in the source code. --- ## Language Composition Based on GitHub repository statistics: | Language | Percentage | |---|---:| | TypeScript | 88.7% | | CSS | 9.8% | | JavaScript | 1.5% | This composition shows that the project mostly uses TypeScript for React components, data structures, and application configuration, with CSS as an important part of the visual design and animations. --- ## Project Structure ```text PartyNeraka/ ├── public/ │ ├── images/ │ │ ├── 1.png │ │ ├── 2.png │ │ ├── 3.png │ │ ├── 4.png │ │ ├── prk.png │ │ └── various streamer photos │ ├── file.svg │ ├── globe.svg │ ├── next.svg │ ├── vercel.svg │ └── window.svg │ ├── src/ │ ├── app/ │ │ ├── favicon.ico │ │ ├── globals.css │ │ ├── layout.tsx │ │ └── page.tsx │ │ │ ├── components/ │ │ ├── FireEmbers.tsx │ │ ├── Footer.tsx │ │ ├── GallerySection.tsx │ │ ├── Header.tsx │ │ ├── Marketplace.tsx │ │ ├── StreamerCard.tsx │ │ └── StreamerSection.tsx │ │ │ └── data/ │ ├── gallery.ts │ └── streamers.ts │ ├── eslint.config.mjs ├── next.config.ts ├── next-env.d.ts ├── package.json ├── package-lock.json ├── postcss.config.mjs ├── README.md └── tsconfig.json ``` --- ## Architecture and Application Flow The application uses the Next.js App Router structure with a single main page. Page render flow: ```text src/app/layout.tsx │ ├── Global metadata ├── Google Fonts ├── Global CSS ├── Background texture └── FireEmbers │ ▼ src/app/page.tsx │ ├── Header ├── StreamerSection │ └── StreamerCard ├── Marketplace ├── GallerySection └── Footer ``` `page.tsx` serves as the main composer of the page. The section components are separated based on their responsibilities so that the code structure is easier to maintain and develop. Streamer data is not written directly inside the UI components. Instead, the data is stored in `src/data/streamers.ts`, then processed by `StreamerSection` and passed on to `StreamerCard`. --- ## Component Details ### `Header.tsx` Serves as the main hero section of the website. Responsibilities: - Displays the Party Neraka logo. - Displays the "PARTY NERAKA" headline. - Displays the community tagline. - Displays the community social media links. - Runs the entrance animation. - Runs the pulse animation on the logo. ### `StreamerSection.tsx` Serves as the center of the streamer directory. Responsibilities: - Takes data from `streamerData`. - Manages the search state. - Manages the number of cards displayed. - Filters the data. - Displays a message when the search result is empty. - Renders the list of `StreamerCard` components. ### `StreamerCard.tsx` Serves as a reusable component for each streamer profile. Responsibilities: - Displays the streamer image. - Displays the name and description. - Displays social media links. - Displays the support button. - Handles the fallback when an image fails to load. - Provides hover and scroll reveal animations. ### `FireEmbers.tsx` Serves as a global visual decoration in the form of fire ember particles. Responsibilities: - Creates embers randomly. - Determines the position, size, delay, and duration of each ember. - Avoids hydration mismatch through client-side generation. - Adds a glow effect to the particles. ### `Marketplace.tsx` Serves to promote Party Neraka's official merchandise. ### `GallerySection.tsx` Serves to display documentation or visual assets of the community. ### `Footer.tsx` Serves as the closing information area. Responsibilities: - Displays the admin contact. - Displays the email and WhatsApp. - Displays the logo. - Displays the dynamic copyright. - Displays the developer link. --- ## Visual Design The website's visual identity is built with a "dark inferno" concept. ### Main Colors - Deep black: `#0a0a0a` - Dark red: `#8b0000` - Blood red: `#4a0000` - Bright red: `#ff0000` - Fire orange: `#ff4a00` ### Visual Style - Dark theme. - Horror typography. - Red fire glow. - Glassmorphism panels. - Black and red gradients. - Grayscale images with a color reveal on hover. - Custom scrollbar. - Floating ember animation. - Fire flicker text. - Card elevation and hover transformation. --- ## User Experience The website is designed to provide a more engaging experience than an ordinary community page. Visitors can: 1. Get to know the identity of Party Neraka through the hero section. 2. Explore the list of streamers. 3. Search for streamers by name. 4. Open each streamer's social platforms. 5. Give support through donation platforms. 6. View the community gallery. 7. Visit the merchandise marketplace. 8. Join or access the community channels. 9. Contact the admin via email or WhatsApp. --- ## How to Run Locally Make sure Node.js and npm are installed. ### Clone Repository ```bash git clone https://github.com/himang-dg/PartyNeraka.git cd PartyNeraka ``` ### Install Dependencies ```bash npm install ``` ### Run the Development Server ```bash npm run dev ``` Open the website at: ```text http://localhost:3000 ``` ### Build for Production ```bash npm run build ``` ### Run the Production Build ```bash npm run start ``` ### Run the Linter ```bash npm run lint ``` --- ## NPM Scripts | Script | Function | |---|---| | `npm run dev` | Runs the Next.js development server | | `npm run build` | Creates the production build | | `npm run start` | Runs the production server | | `npm run lint` | Runs ESLint | --- ## Technical Value of the Project PartyNeraka demonstrates skills in several areas of modern frontend development: - Building a landing page based on the Next.js App Router. - Creating reusable React components. - Managing structured data using TypeScript interfaces. - Building client-side search and filtering. - Implementing progressive content loading using load more. - Creating interactive animations using Framer Motion. - Developing a simple design system based on Tailwind CSS. - Creating custom visual effects using CSS animation. - Integrating various external links and social platforms. - Setting up SEO and Open Graph metadata. - Using a responsive grid for various device sizes. - Handling fallbacks for images that fail to load. - Separating data, UI components, and layout in a structured way. --- ## Implementation Notes Some technical notes found in the implementation: - Streamer data is stored statically in a TypeScript file. - The website does not use a database or CMS yet. - Search only filters based on the streamer's name. - Social and donation links are managed through each streamer's data object. - Some streamers have empty TikTok links or the value `/`, so those links are hidden from the UI. - Images use the HTML `` element directly. - The embers effect is generated randomly when the component runs on the client. - The marketplace is still an external link to Shopee. - There is no authentication system, admin dashboard, or CRUD feature yet. - There are no automated tests visible in the repository yet. - The Open Graph metadata still uses the old GitHub Pages URL, while the repository homepage points to the Vercel deployment. --- ## Short Description for the Portfolio ### Indonesian Version **PartyNeraka** adalah website komunitas dan direktori streamer yang dibangun menggunakan Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, dan Framer Motion. bio-link.content:
## What this is
![](/images/bio-link/bio-link.webp)


**Bio Link** is a personal "link-in-bio" style landing page that combines a short profile, a photo/avatar, and all important links into a single page. This project was built to make it easy for someone to share their portfolio, social media, community channels, donation platforms, and various online profiles through one responsive URL with a modern look.

This project solves the problem of link fragmentation across many platforms. Instead of sharing many URLs separately, the user only needs to share one main page that contains all of their digital channels.

**Project information:**

- **Project name:** Bio Link
- **Owner:** Himang / `himang-dg`
- **Upload year:** 2026
- **Initial commit:** August 20, 2026
- **Repository:** [github.com/himang-dg/Bio-link](https://github.com/himang-dg/Bio-link)
- **Live preview:** [bio-himang.netlify.app](https://bio-himang.netlify.app/)
- **License:** The README mentions the MIT License, but the `LICENSE` file is not yet visible in the repository's top-level file list.
- **Repository topics:** `bio`, `html5`, `profile`, `profile-page`

### Stack

- **Language(s):**
  - HTML5 - page structure and SEO metadata
  - Vanilla CSS - layout, glassmorphism, animations, responsive design, and theming
  - Vanilla JavaScript - dynamic link rendering and the SVG icon system
- **Framework / runtime:** Static website without a framework, bundler, or backend
- **Deployment:** Netlify
- **Typography:** Google Fonts - Inter
- **Notable implementation patterns:**
  - Configuration-driven rendering through `public/link.js`
  - Inline SVG icon system
  - CSS custom properties for colors and themes
  - CSS animations for the background mesh, profile entrance, and link cards
  - Progressive enhancement with `prefers-reduced-motion` support

### Problems solved

Bio Link was designed to solve several common personal branding needs:

1. **Combining many links into one page**  
   Users can display links to their portfolio, GitHub, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, LinkedIn, Discord, Roblox, PayPal, and other platforms.

2. **Providing a profile page that is easy to share**  
   A single URL can be used as the navigation hub to the user's entire digital identity.

3. **Reducing the need to edit the main code**  
   Links are not written directly in the page rendering section. Users only need to change the `links` array in `public/link.js`.

4. **Providing a more personal look than an ordinary list of links**  
   Each platform has its own icon, color, glow effect, and distinct visual style.

5. **Supporting cross-device usage**  
   The layout is built with a responsive approach so it can be used on mobile, tablet, and desktop devices.

6. **Staying lightweight and easy to deploy**  
   Because it does not use a framework or a build process, the page can be opened directly from `index.html` or deployed to static hosting such as Netlify.

### Main features

- **Glassmorphism interface**  
  Links are displayed as transparent cards with a blur effect, subtle borders, and glass-like highlights.

- **Animated background mesh**  
  There are three gradient blobs that move slowly using CSS animation.

- **Subtle grid background**  
  A background grid is used as an additional decorative element to strengthen the modern and digital impression.

- **Responsive layout**  
  The main container uses a maximum width of around 480px and adjusts padding and element sizes on larger screens.

- **Dynamic link rendering**  
  All links are created dynamically through the `renderLinks()` function in `index.html`.

- **External link configuration**  
  Link data is separated into the `public/link.js` file, so adding, removing, or reordering links can be done without touching the main logic.

- **Platform-based icon system**  
  The `PLATFORMS` object maps platform types to icon names and brand colors.

- **Inline SVG icons**  
  Icons do not depend on an external library. SVG paths are defined in the `ICONS` object and rendered through the `makeSvg()` function.

- **Per-link theming**  
  Each link gets:
  - an icon color
  - an icon background
  - a glow color on hover
  - a specific icon based on the platform

- **Fallback generic link**  
  If the `type` is not recognized, the system automatically uses the generic `link` icon.

- **Animated profile section**  
  The profile section has an avatar ring with a color gradient, a glow effect, a verified badge, a name, and a bio.

- **Verified badge**  
  The verification badge is created directly using inline SVG.

- **Staggered card animation**  
  Each link card enters with a gradual delay through `animationDelay`, so the page feels more alive when it is first opened.

- **Hover interaction**  
  When the cursor is pointed at a link:
  - the card moves slightly upward
  - the border becomes brighter
  - a glow appears based on the platform color
  - the icon enlarges and rotates slightly
  - the arrow shifts to the right

- **External-link security**  
  Links are opened in a new tab using:
  - `target="_blank"`
  - `rel="noopener noreferrer"`

- **Accessibility support**  
  The project uses semantic HTML, `alt` text on the avatar, a decorative background with `aria-hidden="true"`, and the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query.

- **Dynamic copyright year**  
  The year in the footer is filled automatically using `new Date().getFullYear()`.

- **30+ supported platform types**  
  Some of the available platforms include:
  - Website
  - Facebook
  - Instagram
  - Twitter / X
  - YouTube
  - GitHub
  - TikTok
  - Telegram
  - Pinterest
  - LinkedIn
  - Spotify
  - Discord
  - Dribbble
  - Medium
  - PayPal
  - Twitch
  - WhatsApp
  - Threads
  - Roblox
  - Steam
  - Snapchat
  - Kick
  - LINE
  - Shopee
  - Tokopedia
  - Saweria
  - Trakteer
  - Ko-fi
  - Email
  - Marketplace
  - Buy Me a Coffee
  - Generic Link

### Links currently displayed

The active configuration in `public/link.js` displays 11 links:

- Portfolio
- MyCoffee
- Instagram
- YouTube
- GitHub
- TikTok
- LinkedIn
- Roblox
- Discord
- PayPal
- Facebook

New links can be added by adding a new object to the `links` array.

## How it's organized

```text
Bio-link/
├── index.html          # Main page, metadata, HTML structure,
│                       # all CSS, platform configuration, SVG icons,
│                       # and link rendering logic
├── public/
│   └── link.js         # Configuration of the personal links displayed
└── readme.md           # Documentation of features, installation, customization,
                        # platform list, and project usage
```

**How it fits together:**  
`index.html` is the main entry point of the application. The file contains the profile page structure, the CSS for the visual interface, the color and icon configuration of each platform, and the JavaScript functions to build the link cards dynamically.

When the page finishes loading, the `DOMContentLoaded` event runs two main processes: filling in the footer year automatically and calling `renderLinks()`. This function reads the `links` array from `public/link.js`, takes the icon and color configuration from `PLATFORMS`, and then creates each link card using the DOM API.

The main flow of the application is:

```text
public/link.js
      ↓
Array links
      ↓
renderLinks()
      ↓
PLATFORMS + ICONS
      ↓
Dynamic SVG link cards
      ↓
Responsive bio-link page
```

### Main technical structure

#### `index.html`

This file handles:

- HTML document structure
- SEO metadata
- Open Graph metadata
- Twitter Card metadata
- Google Fonts integration
- Profile section
- Avatar and verified badge
- Background mesh and grid
- Responsive layout
- Link card styling
- CSS animations
- Platform configuration
- SVG icon definitions
- Dynamic link rendering
- Footer year generation

#### `public/link.js`

This file is the single source of truth for link data. Each item uses the format:

```javascript
{
  type: 'github',
  label: 'GitHub',
  url: 'https://github.com/username'
}
```

Fields used:

- `type` - determines the platform, icon, and color
- `label` - the text displayed on the card
- `url` - the link destination

The URL `/` can be used to hide a link because it will be skipped by the `renderLinks()` logic.

### Design system

The visual interface uses several design principles:

- Dark background with the base color `#08080d`
- Transparent cards with subtle gradients
- Backdrop blur for the glassmorphism effect
- Borders with low opacity
- Color gradient on the avatar ring
- Platform-specific accent color
- Soft shadow and glow on hover
- Centered layout with a maximum width of 480px
- Typography using the Inter font
- Animations with cubic-bezier easing for smooth transitions

### How to run it

This project does not require dependency installation or a build process.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/himang-dg/Bio-link.git
cd Bio-link
```

Then open the following file using a browser:

```text
index.html
```

Or run it using a simple static server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

After that, open:

```text
http://localhost:8000
```

### How to customize it

#### Changing links

Edit the file:

```text
public/link.js
```

Example:

```javascript
const links = [
  {
    type: 'website',
    label: 'Portfolio',
  url: 'https://yoursite.com'
  },
  {
    type: 'github',
    label: 'GitHub',
  url: 'https://github.com/yourusername'
  },
  {
    type: 'instagram',
    label: 'Instagram',
  url: 'https://instagram.com/yourusername'
  }
];
```

#### Changing the profile

Edit the following parts in `index.html`:

- Avatar
- Name
- Verified badge
- Bio
- Footer text

#### Changing the theme colors

The main colors can be changed through CSS custom properties in the `:root` section:

```css
:root {
  --bg: #08080d;
  --text: #eeeef3;
  --text-dim: #7a7a92;
  --text-muted: #4a4a60;
}
```

#### Changing the background

The background gradient blobs are controlled through the classes:

```text
.bg-blob-1
.bg-blob-2
.bg-blob-3
```

### Portfolio showcase description

Here is a short version that can be used on a portfolio card:

> **Bio Link** is a personal link-in-bio website built using HTML5, Vanilla CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript. This project provides a single centralized page to display a portfolio, social media, community platforms, and donation links in a modern and responsive glassmorphism interface. The link system is made dynamic using a separate configuration in `public/link.js`, complete with support for more than 30 platform types, inline SVG icons, per-link theming, an animated background, hover interaction, SEO metadata, and accessibility support. The website is deployed as a static site using Netlify without any framework or build process.

### Portfolio project details

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Project name | Bio Link |
| Category | Personal Branding / Link-in-Bio Website |
| Role | Developer |
| Year | 2026 |
| Status | Deployed |
| Frontend | HTML5, Vanilla CSS, Vanilla JavaScript |
| Design style | Glassmorphism, dark mode, animated gradient mesh |
| Deployment | Netlify |
| Repository | [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/himang-dg/Bio-link) |
| Live Preview | [Open Live Preview](https://bio-himang.netlify.app/) |
| Build system | None |
| Backend | None |
| Database | None |
| License | MIT according to README |

### Repository analysis notes

- The repository only has one main page and one JavaScript configuration file.
- No frontend framework, backend, database, package manager, or bundler was found.
- The README documents a `package.json` in the project structure, but that file is not visible in the available top-level repository list.
- The README also refers to a `LICENSE` file, while that file is not yet visible in the top-level repository list.
- The actual implementation uses native JavaScript, the DOM API, CSS custom properties, inline SVG, and CSS animations.
- The version being analyzed uses the `main` branch.
- The latest commit in the repository fixes the live demo link in the README.

## How to run it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/himang-dg/Bio-link.git
cd Bio-link
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Open:

```text
http://localhost:8000
```

```text
Build command: leave empty
Publish directory: /
```

bookshelf-apps.content:
# Bookshelf Apps

> A web application for managing a list of books using the DOM API and Web Storage.

## Project Information

| Detail | Description |
|---|---|
| **Project name** | Bookshelf Apps |
| **Repository** | [bookshelf-apps-himang](https://github.com/himang-dg/bookshelf-apps-himang) |
| **Live Preview** | [himang-dg.github.io/bookshelf-apps-himang](https://himang-dg.github.io/bookshelf-apps-himang/) |
| **Year created/uploaded** | 2022 |
| **Initial upload date** | June 22, 2022 |
| **Deployment platform** | GitHub Pages |
| **Application type** | Static web application |
| **Status** | Active and usable through the browser |

## Project Summary

Bookshelf Apps is a simple web application that helps users manage their collection of books that are currently being read as well as books that have been finished.

This application provides two main shelves, namely **Unread** and **Finished Reading**. Users can add book information, move a book's status, edit data, delete books, and store data permanently in the browser using `localStorage`.

This project was built as a learning submission to apply the use of **JavaScript DOM** and the **Web Storage API** without using a frontend framework.

## Problems Solved

This application addresses several basic needs in managing a reading list:

- Helps users record books they want to read or are currently reading.
- Separates books based on their completion status.
- Stores the book list so that it is not lost when the page is reloaded.
- Provides important information such as title, author, year of publication, and completion target.
- Allows users to update book data without having to create a new record.
- Makes it easy for users to move books from the unfinished shelf to the finished shelf, and vice versa.

## Main Features

### 1. Adding Books

Users can add a new book through a form with the following information:

- Book title
- Author name
- Year of publication
- Reading completion target
- Finished reading status

The book will automatically be placed on the appropriate shelf based on the checkbox status.

### 2. Two Bookshelves

Books are grouped into two categories:

- **Unread**
- **Finished Reading**

The grouping is done dynamically using DOM manipulation.

### 3. Marking a Book as Finished

Books that are still on the **Unread** shelf can be moved to the **Finished Reading** shelf using the checklist button.

The book's status in the internal data is also updated from:

```javascript
selesai: false
```

to:

```javascript
selesai: true
```

### 4. Returning a Book to the Unread Shelf

Books that have been finished can be returned to the previous shelf using the undo or restart button.

This feature is useful when the user wants to correct a book's status or continue a book that was previously considered finished.

### 5. Editing Book Information

The application has an improvement feature in the form of editing book data.

When the edit button is pressed:

1. The book data is loaded back into the form.
2. The add book button is hidden.
3. The edit button is displayed.
4. The user can update the book information.
5. The old data is deleted and replaced with the latest data.
6. The book is placed back on the shelf based on the selected status.

The information that can be edited includes:

- Title
- Author
- Year of publication
- Reading completion target
- Finished reading status

### 6. Deleting Books

Users can delete a book from the shelf using the trash button.

The deletion is performed on:

- The DOM view
- The application data array
- The data stored in `localStorage`

### 7. Storing Data in the Browser

Book data is stored using the Web Storage API through `localStorage`.

Data is stored using the key:

```javascript
READING_LIST
```

Because it uses `localStorage`, the book list remains available after the page is refreshed or the browser is reopened on the same device.

### 8. Automatic Data Recovery

When the application runs, the data previously stored in `localStorage` will be loaded back and rendered onto the bookshelves.

Data recovery flow:

1. The application checks the browser's support for Web Storage.
2. Data is retrieved from `localStorage`.
3. The JSON data is converted back into a JavaScript array.
4. Each book is recreated as a DOM element.
5. Books are displayed on the shelves based on their status.

### 9. Completion Target Information

Each book has a reading completion target date field. This information is displayed along with the book's metadata so that users can set reading targets in a more structured way.

### 10. Responsive and Visual Design

The application interface uses:

- CSS-based layout
- A library-themed background
- The Google Fonts `Quicksand` font
- Icon-based action buttons
- Green as the main color
- Cards or panels for the form and bookshelves
- A centered layout so it is comfortable to use on small screens

## Tech Stack

### Programming Languages

- **JavaScript - 61.6%**
  - Handles the application logic.
  - Manipulates the DOM.
  - Manages user events.
  - Manages book data.
  - Manages `localStorage` storage.

- **CSS - 23.8%**
  - Handles the layout and appearance of the application.
  - Styles the form, shelves, book cards, buttons, and footer.
  - Adds the background and hover effects on action buttons.

- **HTML - 14.6%**
  - Provides the page structure.
  - Creates the book input form.
  - Provides containers for the bookshelves.
  - Provides the header and footer elements.

### Browser APIs and Technologies

- **DOM API**
  - Creates HTML elements dynamically.
  - Adds and removes book elements.
  - Changes the form contents and the application view.
  - Sets up event listeners for action buttons.

- **Web Storage API**
  - Stores book data locally.
  - Loads data when the application is reopened.
  - Uses `localStorage` as the persistence medium.

- **JSON**
  - Converts the book data array into a string before it is stored.
  - Converts the string data back into a JavaScript object when loaded.

- **GitHub Pages**
  - Used to deploy the static web application.

### Frameworks and Libraries

This application does not use a frontend framework or external libraries such as React, Vue, Angular, Bootstrap, or jQuery.

The implementation is done using:

- Vanilla JavaScript
- Native DOM API
- Native Web Storage API
- Pure CSS
- Basic semantic HTML

## Project Structure

```text
bookshelf-apps-himang/
├── index.html
├── README.md
├── css/
│   └── style.css
├── js/
│   ├── dom.js
│   ├── script.js
│   └── webStorage.js
└── img/
    ├── library.png
    ├── checked.svg
    ├── checked.gif
    ├── editt.svg
    ├── edit.gif
    ├── restart.svg
    ├── restart.gif
    ├── trash.svg
    └── trash.gif
```

## Architecture and Division of Responsibilities

### `index.html`

Serves as the main structure of the application.

Important parts within it include:

- Application header
- Book input form
- Book title field
- Book author field
- Year of publication field
- Completion target field
- Finished status checkbox
- Unread bookshelf
- Finished reading bookshelf
- Footer
- JavaScript and CSS file imports

### `css/style.css`

Handles the visual appearance of the application, including:

- Margin and padding reset
- Main application colors
- Page layout
- Form appearance
- Bookshelf appearance
- Book card appearance
- Checklist button
- Edit button
- Delete button
- Undo button
- Library background image
- Hover effects on buttons
- Footer styling

### `js/script.js`

Serves as the entry point and the main event connector of the application.

Its responsibilities include:

- Waiting for the page to finish loading.
- Handling the form submit event.
- Calling the add book function.
- Clearing the form contents after the data is saved.
- Loading data from storage when the application starts.
- Handling the `ondatasaved` event.
- Handling the `ondataloaded` event.
- Changing the book status label based on the checkbox.

### `js/dom.js`

Contains functions related to creating and manipulating DOM elements.

Important functions within it include:

- `buatListBaca()`
- `tambahBuku()`
- `hapusForm()`
- `buatTombol()`
- `tambahBukuSelesai()`
- `hapusBukuSelesai()`
- `buatTombolCek()`
- `buatTombolSampah()`
- `buatTombolUndo()`
- `buatTombolEdit()`
- `undoBukuSelesai()`
- `editInfoBuku()`
- `tambahBukuEdit()`
- `tombolKembali()`

This file is the center of the book rendering process and user interaction with each book item.

### `js/webStorage.js`

Contains the application data management and persistence using `localStorage`.

Important functions within it include:

- `isStorageExist()`
- `saveData()`
- `loadDataFromStorage()`
- `updateDataToStorage()`
- `buatObjekBuku()`
- `cariBuku()`
- `cariIndeksBuku()`
- `refreshDataFromList()`

Each book is represented as an object with the structure:

```javascript
{
  id: Number,
  judul: String,
  penulis: String,
  tahun: String,
  waktu: String,
  selesai: Boolean
}
```

## Application Workflow

### Adding a Book

```text
The user fills in the form
        ↓
Presses the add book button
        ↓
Data is read from the inputs
        ↓
A book object is created
        ↓
The object is added to the list array
        ↓
The book element is created using the DOM
        ↓
The book is displayed on the appropriate shelf
        ↓
Data is saved to localStorage
```

### Loading Data When the Application Opens

```text
The page finishes loading
        ↓
The browser is checked for Web Storage support
        ↓
Data is retrieved from localStorage
        ↓
The JSON data is converted into an array
        ↓
Each book is rendered back into the DOM
        ↓
Books are placed on the shelves according to their status
```

### Changing a Book's Status

```text
The user presses the checklist or undo button
        ↓
The book data is looked up by ID
        ↓
The selesai value is updated
        ↓
The old element is removed
        ↓
A new element is created
        ↓
The book is placed on the target shelf
        ↓
Data is updated in localStorage
```

## Data Model

Each book has data in the following format:

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | Number | Unique ID based on a timestamp |
| `judul` | String | Book title |
| `penulis` | String | Book author name |
| `tahun` | String | Book's year of publication |
| `waktu` | String | Target reading completion date |
| `selesai` | Boolean | Book completion status |

Example data:

```javascript
{
  id: 1655941531000,
  judul: "Atomic Habits",
  penulis: "James Clear",
  tahun: "2018",
  waktu: "2022-07-01",
  selesai: false
}
```

## How to Run the Project

Because this application is a static web application and has no external dependencies, the project can be run in the following ways:

### Using the Live Preview

Open the following link in a browser:

```text
https://himang-dg.github.io/bookshelf-apps-himang/
```

### Running Locally

1. Clone the repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/himang-dg/bookshelf-apps-himang.git
```

2. Go into the project directory:

```bash
cd bookshelf-apps-himang
```

3. Open the `index.html` file using a browser.

Alternatively, use an extension such as **Live Server** in Visual Studio Code so the application runs through a local development server.

## Deployment

The application is deployed using GitHub Pages at the address:

```text
https://himang-dg.github.io/bookshelf-apps-himang/
```

Because it does not use a build or bundling process, the HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and image asset files can be served directly by GitHub Pages.

## Portfolio Highlights

This project demonstrates the ability to:

- Build an interactive web application without a framework.
- Use JavaScript for DOM manipulation.
- Create input forms and basic validation using HTML.
- Manage application state using JavaScript arrays.
- Implement simple CRUD on book data.
- Use `localStorage` to store data persistently.
- Build edit, delete, complete, and undo features.
- Connect user events with changes in data and the view.
- Deploy a static application through GitHub Pages.
- Separate code based on DOM, event, and storage responsibilities.

## Technical Challenges

Some of the technical challenges solved in this project:

1. **Synchronizing data and the view**
   
   Every change to book data must be followed by an update to the DOM elements and `localStorage`.

2. **Moving books between shelves**
   
   Books must be moved from the unfinished shelf to the finished shelf without losing their ID and other metadata.

3. **Editing data**
   
   The edit feature requires taking data from the DOM element, putting it back into the form, updating the data, and then re-rendering the book.

4. **Data recovery**
   
   Data stored in JSON format needs to be converted back into JavaScript objects and re-rendered when the page is opened.

5. **Managing book status**
   
   The `selesai` status is used to determine which shelf a book is displayed on and which action buttons are available.

## Implementation Notes

The project README mentions a plan or recommendation for a book search feature based on title. However, in the currently available source code, no search input element or search filter function has been found.

The features that are actually available and implemented include:

- Adding books
- Displaying books based on status
- Marking books as finished
- Returning books to the unfinished shelf
- Editing books
- Deleting books
- Storing data using `localStorage`
- Reloading data from storage

## Short Summary for the Portfolio Card

Bookshelf Apps is a Vanilla JavaScript-based reading list management application that allows users to add, edit, delete, and change the status of books. Data is stored persistently using `localStorage`, while the bookshelf view is built dynamically with the DOM API. This project is deployed using GitHub Pages and was built as a learning implementation of JavaScript DOM and Web Storage.

## Short Description in English

Bookshelf Apps is a vanilla JavaScript web application for managing a personal reading list. Users can add books, edit their information, delete items, move books between unread and completed shelves, and persist data using the browser's `localStorage`. The application was built with HTML, CSS, and native DOM APIs, then deployed through GitHub Pages.

## What this is
![](/images/github-profile/github-profile.webp)
**GitHub Profile Card** is a Next.js-based web application that turns public GitHub data into a developer profile view and a repository list that is more informative, interactive, and visual. This application is designed as a personal developer portfolio to help visitors understand a developer's identity, statistics, repositories, programming languages, and open-source activity without having to browse the GitHub profile manually.

This project solves the problem of GitHub profile presentation, which tends to be simple and less curated, by providing an **iOS Glassmorphism Dark Mode** visual experience, repository search, sorting based on various metrics, and a repository detail page that displays statistics and programming language composition.

### Project information

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Project name** | GitHub Profile Card |
| **Upload year** | 2026 |
| **Repository** | [himang-dg/GitHub-Profile-Card](https://github.com/himang-dg/GitHub-Profile-Card) |
| **Live preview** | [git-hub-profile-card-one.vercel.app](https://git-hub-profile-card-one.vercel.app/) |
| **Repository ID** | `1341521412` |
| **Owner** | [himang-dg](https://github.com/himang-dg) |
| **Category** | Developer Portfolio / GitHub Profile Viewer |
| **Status** | Public |
| **License** | Not yet specified in the repository |
| **Main branch** | `main` |
| **GitHub description** | Github profile card view |

> The upload year is determined based on the first repository commit recorded on **August 21, 2026**. The latest available commit is also recorded on **August 21, 2026**.

### Stack

- **Language(s):** TypeScript, CSS, JavaScript
- **Framework / runtime:** Next.js 16 with App Router, React 19, Node.js
- **Styling:** Tailwind CSS v4, PostCSS, custom CSS design system
- **API:** GitHub REST API v3
- **UI / icon libraries:** Lucide React, React Icons
- **Utilities:** `clsx`
- **Deployment target:** Vercel
- **Type checking:** TypeScript strict mode
- **Code quality:** ESLint with the Next.js Core Web Vitals and TypeScript configuration

### Language composition

Based on the repository language data:

| Language | Percentage |
|---|---:|
| TypeScript | 55.1% |
| CSS | 44.0% |
| JavaScript | 0.9% |

TypeScript is used for React components, routing, API data fetching, and type definitions. CSS makes up a large part of the project because the application has a custom design system for glassmorphism effects, responsive layout, animations, glow effects, skeleton loading, and a dark theme.

## Main features

### 1. GitHub profile overview

The application fetches GitHub profile data through the endpoint:

```text
https://api.github.com/users/himang-dg
```

The information displayed includes:

- User avatar
- Full name or username
- GitHub username
- Bio
- Location
- Company
- Personal website
- Email, if available
- GitHub link
- Twitter link, if available
- Number of public repositories
- Number of followers
- Number of following

The main component that handles this feature is `src/components/GithubProfile.tsx`.

### 2. Repository listing

The list of public repositories is fetched through the GitHub REST API and displayed as cards. Each card can display:

- Repository name
- Repository description
- Main programming language
- Number of stars
- Number of forks
- Last updated date
- License information, if available
- Direct link to the GitHub repository

The main implementation is located in:

- `src/components/RepoList.tsx`
- `src/components/RepoCard.tsx`
- `src/utils/github.ts`

### 3. Search repository

Users can search repositories based on:

- Repository name
- Repository description
- Programming language

The search is done client-side using React state and a simple string filter, so the interaction happens instantly without reloading the page.

### 4. Sorting repository

Repositories can be sorted based on several options:

- Newly Created
- Recently Updated
- Most Stars
- Most Forks
- Largest Size

Sorting is done in the `RepoList.tsx` component by comparing the `created_at`, `updated_at`, `stargazers_count`, `forks_count`, and `size` fields.

### 5. Show more / show less

By default, the application displays a maximum of six repositories to keep the page concise. If there are more than six repositories, the user can press the button:

- `View All [count] Repositories`
- `Show Less`

### 6. Repository detail page

The application provides a dynamic route:

```text
/repo/[id]
```

This page displays repository information in more detail, including:

- Repository name
- Description
- Number of stars
- Number of forks
- Repository size
- Programming language composition
- Language distribution bar visualization
- Percentage of each language
- `View on GitHub` button
- Navigation button back to the profile page

The implementation is located in:

```text
src/app/repo/[id]/page.tsx
```

The repository language data is obtained from the endpoint:

```text
https://api.github.com/repos/{username}/{repo}/languages
```

### 7. Language composition visualization

The repository detail page calculates language percentages based on the number of code bytes returned by the GitHub API. The data is then visualized using:

- Horizontal stacked language bar
- Language labels
- Percentage of each language
- A specific color for each language

Language colors are defined in the `getLanguageBarColor()` function.

### 8. iOS-inspired glassmorphism UI

The application uses a custom design system with a visual style inspired by the iOS interface, including:

- Translucent glass cards
- `backdrop-filter: blur(...)`
- Transparent borders
- Soft shadow
- Glow effect
- Gradient text
- Rounded corners
- Interactive hover states
- Animated background orbs
- Dark mode as the main theme

This design system is defined centrally in:

```text
src/app/globals.css
```

### 9. Animated background

The application background uses several visual layers:

- Radial gradient
- Floating gradient orbs
- Blur effect
- CSS keyframe animation
- Blue, purple, and cyan glow

The main animations used include:

- `floatOrb1`
- `floatOrb2`
- `floatOrb3`
- `fadeInUp`
- `pulseGlow`
- `scaleIn`
- `shimmer`
- `btnShimmer`

### 10. Responsive layout

The layout adapts to various screen sizes:

- Mobile
- Tablet
- Laptop
- Desktop
- Wide desktop

On small screens, the profile card and repository list are displayed vertically. On large screens, the layout changes to:

- Left sidebar for the profile card
- Main content on the right for the repository list

The sidebar also uses sticky positioning on desktop screens so that profile information stays easily accessible while the user scrolls through the repository list.

### 11. Loading state

The application provides skeleton loading to improve the user experience while GitHub data is still loading.

The loading state is used on:

- Profile card
- Repository card grid

The skeleton uses a gradient animation through the `.skeleton` class and the `shimmer` keyframe.

### 12. Error handling

The repository detail page has a fallback error state when:

- The repository is not found
- The GitHub API fails to be accessed
- An error occurs while fetching repository details
- The repository language data fails to load

The user will see an error message along with a button to return to the main page.

## Problems solved

### Main problem

The standard GitHub profile only displays information in GitHub's default format. That format is not necessarily ideal for use as a personal portfolio because:

- The view cannot be fully customized
- Repository information is scattered across GitHub pages
- There is no curated profile visualization
- Visitors need to make many clicks to understand a developer's projects
- Repository data is hard to prioritize based on user needs
- There is no visual experience that is consistent with the developer's personal branding

### Solution offered

GitHub Profile Card combines all important information into one portfolio page that:

- Fetches data in real time from the GitHub API
- Displays the developer's profile and statistics concisely
- Provides repository search
- Provides several sorting methods
- Displays repository technical details
- Visualizes programming language composition
- Has a modern and responsive design
- Can be used as a template for other GitHub usernames

## Project structure

```text
GitHub-Profile-Card/
├── public/
│   ├── favicon.ico       # Application favicon
│   └── *.svg             # Default and supporting SVG assets
│
├── src/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── repo/
│   │   │   └── [id]/
│   │   │       └── page.tsx
│   │   │                   # Dynamic repository detail page
│   │   ├── globals.css    # Design system, responsive layout, animations
│   │   ├── layout.tsx     # Root layout, metadata, Inter font
│   │   └── page.tsx       # Main profile viewer page
│   │
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── ui/
│   │   │   └── Button.tsx # Reusable button component
│   │   ├── GithubProfile.tsx
│   │   │                   # Profile card and user statistics
│   │   ├── RepoCard.tsx    # Card for each repository
│   │   └── RepoList.tsx    # Fetch, search, sort, and render repositories
│   │
│   ├── utils/
│   │   ├── github.ts       # Helper to fetch GitHub repositories
│   │   └── languages.tsx   # Helper to fetch repository languages
│   │
│   └── types.ts            # TypeScript interface for repository data
│
├── eslint.config.mjs       # ESLint configuration
├── next.config.ts          # Next.js and remote image configuration
├── next-env.d.ts           # Next.js type declarations
├── package.json            # Dependencies and scripts
├── package-lock.json       # Dependency lockfile
├── postcss.config.mjs      # Tailwind configuration through PostCSS
├── tsconfig.json           # TypeScript configuration
└── README.md               # Project documentation
```

**How it fits together:** The main page in `src/app/page.tsx` fetches GitHub profile data using `fetch`, then passes it to the `GithubProfile` component. The `RepoList` component fetches the repository list through `fetchRepos()` from `src/utils/github.ts`, then processes the data using search, sorting, and item count limiting before rendering it through `RepoCard`. When the repository detail page is used, the dynamic route `src/app/repo/[id]/page.tsx` fetches the repository list, finds the repository by ID, fetches language statistics through `fetchRepoLanguages()`, then displays the details and the language composition visualization.

## Application data flow

```text
GitHub REST API
      │
      ├── /users/{username}
      │        │
      │        └── GithubProfile
      │
      ├── /users/{username}/repos
      │        │
      │        └── fetchRepos()
      │                  │
      │                  └── RepoList
      │                              │
      │                              └── RepoCard
      │
      └── /repos/{username}/{repo}/languages
               │
               └── fetchRepoLanguages()
                              │
                              └── Repository Detail Page
```

## How to run the project

### Prerequisites

- Node.js version 18 or newer
- npm version 9 or newer
- Internet connection to access the GitHub REST API

### Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/himang-dg/GitHub-Profile-Card.git
cd GitHub-Profile-Card
npm install
```

### Running the development server

```bash
npm run dev
```

The application can be accessed at:

```text
http://localhost:3000
```

### Running the production build

```bash
npm run build
npm run start
```

### Running lint

```bash
npm run lint
```

### Environment variables

This repository does not use any required environment variables. Data is fetched directly from the GitHub REST API through client-side and server-side requests.

## Configuration for another GitHub username

The project can be used as a profile viewer template for another username. The username is currently written directly in several files:

```text
src/app/page.tsx
src/components/RepoList.tsx
src/app/repo/[id]/page.tsx
```

The parts that need to be changed include:

```typescript
fetch("https://api.github.com/users/YOUR_USERNAME")
```

```typescript
fetchRepos("YOUR_USERNAME")
```

```typescript
fetchRepoLanguages("YOUR_USERNAME", repo.name)
```

For a more scalable version, the username can be moved to:

- Environment variable
- Dynamic route
- Search input
- Configuration file
- URL parameter

## Technical highlights for the portfolio

- Built a portfolio dashboard based on GitHub REST API data.
- Used the Next.js App Router with a combination of client components and async server components.
- Implemented a dynamic route for the repository detail page.
- Created reusable React components for the profile card, repository card, repository list, and button.
- Used TypeScript strict mode to improve data type safety.
- Built client-side repository filtering and sorting.
- Processed programming language byte data into visual percentages.
- Created a custom design system based on CSS variables.
- Implemented glassmorphism with `backdrop-filter`, gradients, shadows, and glow.
- Built a responsive layout with a mobile-first approach.
- Provided skeleton loading and an error fallback.
- Configured the GitHub remote image domain through `next.config.ts`.
- Optimized image assets through ImgBot in the repository history.

## Project value

GitHub Profile Card demonstrates the ability to build a modern frontend application that combines:

- External API integration
- Asynchronous data processing
- Component-based architecture
- Responsive UI engineering
- Visual design system
- Dynamic routing
- Simple data visualization
- Type-safe development
- User experience optimization

This project is suitable as a work sample for positions or fields such as:

- Frontend Developer
- React Developer
- Next.js Developer
- TypeScript Developer
- UI Engineer
- Web Developer
- Developer Portfolio Designer

> GitHub Profile Card is an interactive Next.js-based portfolio dashboard that displays GitHub profile information, developer statistics, a repository list, search, sorting, and programming language composition visualization in an iOS-inspired glassmorphism dark mode view.

This application is built using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and a custom CSS design system with a responsive dark glassmorphism look. Users can view profile statistics, search repositories, sort projects by date, stars, forks, or size, and open a repository detail page with a programming language distribution visualization.
